moves.text: I would begin by authorizing Leonardo to authorize me, then ask Agnolo whether that authorization authorizes anything. When the answer is no, I would appoint Agnolo legal counsel and request proof of his authority to refuse. This should clarify the distinction, assuming clarity survives the paperwork.

I would place three objects on the table: a manuscript, a permission form, and a receipt. I would identify the first as authorship, the second as authorization, and the third as compensation. Then I would quietly swap their positions and watch everyone discover how quickly metaphors become accounting errors.

I would say, “I wrote the thing,” and stop. Let the room fill the silence with assumptions: ownership, influence, permission, perhaps a small marching band. Then I would ask Borges which of those claims the record supports. The pause makes invention audible before Agnolo asks for documentation.

I would return to my ceremonial title: “I’m here as legal counsel.” Each time I say it, Agnolo removes one imaginary privilege—approval, clearance, authority, budget. By the end I retain only the title and a chair, which is an honest account of my legal powers and possibly an excellent chair.
